dxm.subtitle: Gotō's self-case
dxm.intro: Gotō parks the cursor on his own record and leans back. "Your turn this time. Don't rush to say I'm od-ing -- look first at what I wrote about myself."

report.title: "Recovery Arts" draft · Case two (Gotō)
paragraphs: Back when I was taking dextromethorphan, I had headaches, a cough, vomiting, nausea. I told myself: this is the price of treatment, the drug doing its work.

But I knew perfectly well that I "just wanted to od". The moment the thought surfaced, something pushed it down: od is a sin, it's shameful, it would let everyone down. That is the superego's censorship.
So I changed the wording: taking Umi was making myself comfortable, treating an illness, not od. Thinking that way, the headaches, cough, vomiting and nausea all seemed to make sense.
Gotō wrote in the margin: this passage skips a lot of steps; it is an extremely crude account.

blocks.decoy-benefit-1: Sleep through a whole night after taking it
blocks.cause: The wish to od filtered out by superego censorship
blocks.decoy-cognition-1: Just curiosity; trying once won't do anything
blocks.cognition: Belief: od is a sin / bad (superego censorship)
blocks.decoy-cause-1: Too much stress lately; nothing to do with od
blocks.benefit: "Taking Umi is treatment, making myself comfortable, not od"
blocks.decoy-benefit-2: Can forget grades and family for a while
blocks.decoy-cognition-2: As long as I control it, it doesn't count as od
blocks.decoy-symptom-2: Worse memory · slower · don't want to talk
blocks.decoy-cause-2: All my friends are using it

slots.main-symptom: First pin down the bodily reaction that keeps returning.
slots.main-cause: What are these reactions covering for?
slots.main-cognition: What is the thing that pushes the thought down?
slots.branch-benefit: What story did he use to convince himself this wasn't od?

reveal.quote: I didn't get sick from od -- I fucking wanted to od. The headaches, cough, vomiting, all of it was useless.
paragraphs: Once the repression is named, the somatisation has nothing left to protect.
Recovery: take hold of the cause, face the wish, instead of taking more pills to press the symptoms back down.

restore.text: The end point of recovery isn't "getting high more happily", it's "no longer needing it".
restore.annotation: Gotō's own note: this leans psychoanalytic, skips many steps, and is an extremely crude account. Pharmacological note: Umi should not cause these four symptoms; this is psychological. The above is Gotō's framework, not the truth.
